intro: You're searching for mirror wills near you, which usually means you and your partner want wills that reflect your shared plans for each other and your family. Finding a local wills and probate specialist can help you put those plans in place properly, with the reassurance of speaking to someone face to face.
need_heading: What people searching for mirror wills near me usually need
need_lead: Most people looking for mirror wills want a straightforward way to make sure their partner is provided for and their wishes are clear.
needs: You're a couple who want almost identical wills leaving everything to each other, then to the same beneficiaries.
You want to avoid the uncertainty of dying without a will, which can leave your partner in a difficult position.
You have children or grandchildren and want to think about how they would be provided for.
You'd prefer to discuss your options with a local professional rather than sort it all out online.
You want to understand how mirror wills work and whether they are right for your circumstances.
context_heading: One key thing to understand about mirror wills
context: Mirror wills are two separate wills with almost identical terms, usually made by a couple. Each will typically leaves everything to the other, and then to the same beneficiaries. It's important to know that either person can change their will later, so mirror wills are not set in stone.

Writing a will is not a reserved legal activity in England and Wales, so some will writers are not regulated. Solicitors (regulated by the SRA) and chartered legal executives (regulated by CILEx) are regulated, insured and covered by the Legal Ombudsman. When choosing a provider, ask whether they are regulated, whether they hold professional indemnity insurance and where your original will is stored. If you live in Scotland, make sure your adviser practises in the right jurisdiction, as Scotland has its own rules on succession.

faqs.a: Mirror wills are two separate wills, usually made by a couple, with almost identical terms. They typically leave everything to each other and then to the same beneficiaries.

faqs.q: Can we change our mirror wills later?
faqs.a: Yes, either person can change their will later. Mirror wills are not legally binding on each other in the way that mutual wills can be.

faqs.q: Are mirror wills suitable if we have children?
faqs.a: Mirror wills can include arrangements for children, such as appointing guardians and setting up trusts. A specialist can help you consider the best way to protect your children's interests.

faqs.q: Do we need a solicitor to make mirror wills?
faqs.a: Writing a will is not a reserved legal activity in England and Wales, so you can use a regulated solicitor or an unregulated will writer. Using a regulated professional gives you the reassurance of insurance and access to the Legal Ombudsman if something goes wrong.

extra_heading: What your search for mirror wills near you suggests
extra: Searching for mirror wills near me usually means you and your partner want to put wills in place together, with the same terms, and you'd rather deal with someone local you can sit down with. You might be newly married or living together, or you may be updating older wills after a change in your family. Either way, you want a straightforward conversation about how mirror wills work for the two of you.

When you speak to a professional, they will likely ask about your relationship status, your children, and how you own your home, because these details affect how mirror wills should be drafted. They may also explain the difference between mirror wills and mutual wills, which are rarer and can restrict each person's ability to change their will later. This first conversation is your chance to ask about regulation, insurance and where your original wills will be stored.

It's worth remembering that mirror wills are two separate wills, so either of you can change your own will in the future without the other's consent. That flexibility is often what couples want, but it's important to understand it from the start. A local specialist can talk you through how to keep your plans aligned as your circumstances change.

extra_faqs.q: Do mirror wills have to be made at the same time?
extra_faqs.a: Not necessarily. Mirror wills are two separate wills, so they can be made at different times, though couples often make them together. What matters is that the terms mirror each other, leaving everything to each other and then to the same beneficiaries.

extra_faqs.q: Can we use mirror wills if we're not married?
extra_faqs.a: Yes, mirror wills can be used by any couple, whether married, in a civil partnership or living together. However, the legal effect can differ, especially for unmarried couples, so it's important to discuss your situation with a specialist.
